summary: Energy infrastructure buildout for AI data centers is solvable — turbine capacity, natural gas, and capitalism will meet demand; political headwinds are the real constraint
summary_extended: Baker argues that the physical energy infrastructure challenge for AI data centers is fundamentally solvable through American capitalism and engineering ingenuity, and that investors should not fear the power buildout as a bottleneck. He cites specific evidence: turbine manufacturers including GE Vernova, Siemens Energy, Caterpillar, and Cummins are already running 24-hour production shifts to meet demand, and repurposing jet engines from retired aircraft as turbines has become a growing business line. Natural gas is the primary near-term fuel source, with solar and nuclear viable over longer horizons. Baker's contrarian structural view is that the real constraint on AI data center buildout is not physical or engineering capacity but rather regulatory and political headwinds — meaning the investment risk is misdiagnosed by the market, and the companies supplying turbines and power generation equipment are well-positioned as direct beneficiaries of sustained demand.
detail: Baker argues America's capitalism and engineering capacity will solve the physical buildout challenge. Turbine manufacturers (GE Vernova, Siemens Energy, Caterpillar, Cummins) are running 24-hour shifts. Jet engines being repurposed from old planes as turbines is a growing business. Natural gas is the near-term fuel. Solar/nuclear viable longer term. The real constraint is regulatory/political, not physical.
